title: Income Sources & The $0-Earned-Income Question
subtitle: Kalshi event contracts · rental income · savings interest · property management

sections.title: 1. The short answer
sections.intro: Three separate questions are routinely conflated. They have different answers, and the middle one is the one that matters.

c: Does this income count as “earned income” for tax and benefit purposes?
NO. Interest, rents and capital gains are unearned income.
IRS: “Unearned income. This is investment-type income and includes interest, dividends and capital gains, rents, royalties, etc.”
Does this income count toward the $580/month community-engagement income test?
YES. The test is measured on MAGI-based household income, which is built from adjusted gross income and therefore includes unearned income.
42 CFR §435.552(f)(2) · 42 CFR §435.603(e) · WIC §14005.69(e)(6) · DHCS member letter: “Have an income from any source of at least $580”
Can the hours spent trading or managing rentals count as “work” hours?
Probably for property management; unverified for trading. CMS expressly says self-employment counts. No official guidance names rental-property management or prediction-market trading.
CMS IFC preamble §II.C.1 · 42 CFR §435.552(b). Flagged F-02, F-03.

sections.title: 2. IRS classification of each income type

c: Wages, salaries, tips, other taxable employee pay
“Earned income includes … Wages, salaries, tips and other taxable employee pay”
“Net earnings from self-employment”; “Earned income includes all the taxable income and wages from working either as an employee or from running or owning a business.”
Union strike benefits; long-term disability benefits received prior to minimum retirement age; gross income as a statutory employee
“It also includes certain other types of taxable income … Union strike benefits … Long-term disability benefits received prior to minimum retirement age”

“Unearned income. This is investment-type income and includes interest, dividends and capital gains, rents, royalties, etc. Distributions of interest, dividends, capital gains and other unearned income from a trust are also unearned income to a beneficiary of the trust.”

“Rental real estate income generally isn’t included in net earnings from self-employment subject to self-employment tax and is generally subject to the passive activity limits.” Basic reporting form: Schedule E (Form 1040).
Rental activity where you provide substantial services, or you are a real estate dealer
Reported on Schedule C as a business

“If you make this election, you must report rental real estate income on Schedule E (or Schedule C, if you provide substantial services).” Schedule C instructions: use “Schedule E (Form 1040) to report rental real estate and royalty income or (loss) that is not subject to self-employment tax.”
“Investment income isn’t subject to self-employment tax.”
Not self-employment income, even though trading is a trade or business
“Gains and losses from selling securities from being a trader aren’t subject to self-employment tax.” Business expenses are reported on Schedule C.

sections.title: 3. The IRS “trader” test — and why it still does not create earned income
sections.intro: IRS Topic No. 429 sets the official test. A full-time trader may well satisfy it. It does not change the character of the income.

c: All three conditions must be met

“To be engaged in business as a trader in securities, you must meet all of the following conditions: • You must seek to profit from daily market movements in the prices of securities and not from dividends, interest, or capital appreciation; • Your activity must be substantial; and • You must carry on the activity with continuity and regularity.”

“Typical holding periods for securities bought and sold; The frequency and dollar amount of your trades during the year; The extent to which you pursue the activity to produce income for a livelihood; and The amount of time you devote to the activity.”
“It doesn’t matter whether you call yourself a trader or a day trader, you’re an investor for Federal income tax purposes.”
It is a trade or business

“Special rules apply if you’re a trader in securities, in the business of buying and selling securities for your own account. The law considers this to be a trade or business, even though a trader doesn’t maintain an inventory and doesn’t have customers.”

Traders may elect §475(f) mark-to-market. Without a valid election, gains and losses are capital and go on Schedule D and Form 8949. With a timely valid election they are generally ordinary and go on Form 4797 Part II. The election must be made “by the due date (not including extensions) of the tax return for the year prior to the year for which you intend the election to become effective.”

“under section 475(c)(2), the term security includes a share of stock, beneficial ownership interests in certain partnerships and trusts, evidence of indebtedness, and certain notional principal contracts, as well as evidence of an interest in, or a derivative financial instrument in, any of these items and certain identified hedges of these items.” Whether CFTC event contracts fall inside this definition is not settled by any official source located in this session — flagged F-04.

sections.title: 4. What Kalshi itself officially reports
sections.intro: Verified directly from Kalshi's own help-centre article. This is the only non-government source used anywhere on this site, and it is used solely for what the platform says about itself.

c: “contains transaction proceeds from broker transactions (crypto transfers)”

“summarizes your trading activity including profits, losses, and fees.” Access: Kalshi → Account → Tax Info → select year → download. “We use the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) accounting method to compute profits and losses.” Updated on the first of each month.
Yes — but it is not an IRS information return.

“This information and the information included in the Profit and Loss statement are not tax advice, and Kalshi cannot give members advice on their taxes. It is intended as a tool to assist members, but as always, each member should consult with a tax professional for any questions and is responsible for ensuring the accuracy of all returns.”

“Some tax forms will be delivered electronically — check your email for a delivery from Zenwork, our tax form provider.” “If no 1099 forms appear in your account, it is likely because you did not meet the IRS thresholds required for issuance.”

BLANK — no official IRS guidance located. No Revenue Ruling, Notice, or regulation classifying Kalshi/CFTC event-contract income was found. Four competing treatments appear only in unofficial practitioner literature (Section 1256 / Form 6781; capital asset / Schedule D + Form 8949; ordinary income / Schedule 1 line 8z; gambling income). None is published here as verified.

sections.title: 6. Whose income counts — household vs individual

c: “The agency must determine the monthly income based on the individual’s MAGI-based income, for their MAGI-based household, as defined at §435.603.”

Taxpayer who expects to file and not be claimed as a dependent: the taxpayer plus everyone they expect to claim as a tax dependent. Married couples living together are each included in the other’s household regardless of filing status.
When converting income to hours the agency “must use a reasonable method to allocate work hours between members of the household.”

“All individuals must independently meet the participation criteria; one individual’s compliance cannot be used to satisfy another’s requirement.” The worked example in ACWDL 25-30 concerns hours (a partner’s 100 work hours cannot satisfy the applicant’s requirement). The same letter defines the income criterion as “an individual’s total gross income for a month”.
How a county applies a household MAGI income figure against an individual-level compliance determination is not spelled out. Left unresolved — flagged F-01. Do not assume either reading.

For MAGI-determined individuals the agency “must not … apply any assets or resources test”. Owning rental property, a brokerage balance or savings does not disqualify a person from MAGI adult-group Medi-Cal.

sections.title: 7. Converting income to hours when a month falls below $580

c: “If the monthly income is less than the applicable Federal minimum wage requirement … multiplied by 80 hours, and the agency does not have documentation regarding the number of hours worked, the agency may calculate the hours for work … based on the monthly income as determined under paragraph (f)(2) … provided that the agency must use a reasonable method to allocate work hours between members of the household.”
“the agency must calculate the hours for work by dividing the monthly income as determined under paragraph (f)(2) … by the applicable Federal minimum wage requirement under 29 U.S.C. 206(a)(1)(C).”

“After the agency determines an applicable individual’s hours for work, completing community service, participating in a work program, and less than half-time enrollment in an educational program, the hours must be added together. Adding the hours will provide the total hours for the combined activities.”

“The hours for work …, community service …, and participating in a work program … must be determined separately and based on the time spent on the specific activity in such month.” And CMS: “this option must only be used when the monthly income is less than the applicable Federal minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours and the State does not have information regarding the number of hours worked.”
A State “may not combine educational program hours with another activity if the individual is enrolled in an educational program at least half-time.”

sections.title: 8. Do trading or property-management hours count as “work”?

c: Managing property for a fee, for third-party owners
Ordinary self-employment / a trade or business. The hours count as work and the fee income is earned income and self-employment income.
Managing rental property you own — collecting rent, arranging repairs, screening tenants

“Work” is defined as work in exchange for money, in-kind work for goods or services, and unpaid work other than community service. CMS states that self-employment from “starting a business, owning a business, or as an independent contractor” meets that definition and that “the hours the individual spends performing these duties would count toward meeting the 80-hour requirement.” But no official CMS, DHCS or county document uses the words “landlord”, “rental property” or “property manager”.
Reasonable reading — not squarely addressed. Flagged F-02. Confirm with the county before relying on it.
Managing property in exchange for free or reduced rent
Would appear to fall inside “work in exchange for goods or services (‘in-kind’ work)”, but no official example addresses it.

No official federal or California Medicaid guidance, and no IRS ruling, addresses prediction-market or event-contract trading in the community-engagement context. Two independent obstacles: (a) it is unresolved whether event contracts are “securities” for IRC §475(c)(2), so the IRS trader framework may not apply at all; (b) even if it does, IRS Topic No. 429 says trader gains “aren’t subject to self-employment tax”.
UNVERIFIED — cannot be confirmed from any official source. Flagged F-03, F-04. Left blank.

sections.title: 9. Volatility and documentation risk for trading + rental income

c: The federal income test is applied to “a month in the period under §435.556(a)”. California requires compliance in any one month since the last renewal, and DHCS tells members they can meet it by having the income “in any month since your last renewal”.
Materially protective. One qualifying month out of six is enough in California.
Adult-group financial eligibility is MAGI ≤138% FPL. The budget period may be current monthly or projected annual at state election (§435.603(h)).
A large trading gain can push MAGI over the Medi-Cal limit → Medi-Cal ends → Covered California special enrolment. Analysis — a scenario, not a quoted rule.

Covered California: “Beginning with the 2026 tax year (filed in 2027), people who get too much financial help may need to pay back the full amount they owe. It will no longer be capped based on income.”
Under-estimating MAGI when trading gains are volatile now carries unlimited repayment exposure.

Covered California: “Effective Date: Jan. 1, 2028 — You’ll need to prove that you qualify for financial help before you get it. Financial help won’t be applied while your information is being reviewed or updated. If you don’t confirm or update your information, you won’t be automatically re-enrolled with financial help for the next plan year.”
Plan for documentation, not just for dollars.
Kalshi lists four 1099s — none reports event-contract trading profit. The PnL statement is “not tax advice” and is not an IRS information return.

The person must be able to document MAGI from their own records, because a county may request documentation when its reliable data sources are unavailable or “not reasonably compatible” (§435.557(b)(2)).

26 U.S.C. §45R(d)(5)(B): a seasonal worker is one who “performs labor or services on a seasonal basis as defined by the Secretary of Labor, including workers covered by section 500.20(s)(1) of title 29, Code of Federal Regulations and retail workers employed exclusively during holiday seasons.” DHCS describes the same criterion more loosely as being for “individuals with fluctuating income” and “people whose hours change frequently or who have seasonal jobs”.
Do not rely on the averaging rule. Rely on the single-month test. State guidance is broader than the federal cross-reference — flagged F-05.
